basis: Exact source solids and original world-space triangle meshes. Continuous native BREP conservative sweeps of every original rigid-module solid against every remaining original obstacle. Continuous triangle translation for other straight movers. Independently validated conservative axisymmetric BREP swept envelopes for declared fasteners, with original driver-envelope checks preserved.
limitations: This receipt does not change the hosted assembly-path tool result.
Native BREP volume checks establish nominal geometric clearance. They do not model friction, thread deformation, torque, cable flex, or hands.
The 17 manufacturer Pico solids and two specified soldered header rows form one rigid module. Their fabrication and solder joints are preconditions, not new user-removal steps.
The base is held for the documented device assembly phase. Approximate support checks record any additional holds.
Physical print, fit, cable and repeated-assembly qualification is unperformed.

Local watertight mesh validation, not BREP or hardware acceptance. Positive-travel contact is conservatively blocked; starting contact may also block sliding. Mesh tessellation approximates curves. Straight translation and declared helical fastener motion only; no mate solving, deformation, thread engagement or torque. Press/snap fits are declared, never simulated. Tool reach is a swept-envelope approximation, not a driver drawing. Static stability is approximate: a centre-of-mass projection onto a support polygon of mesh contacts with already-stable parts, not gravity simulation, friction, tipping or fixture analysis. A needs-hold finding names an external hold the model cannot prove. Subassembly and multi-part moves are heuristic, not exhaustive. Sampling paths are found-by-search, never proven. Blocked and unknown parts are not "impossible".
